entry: window.M.call(name, args) → Promise<{ok, tool, ms, result|error}>

tools.name: analysis.bitplane
tools.description: Show one bit plane of an image: every pixel becomes white if the chosen bit (0 = least significant … 7 = most significant) of the chosen channel is set, black otherwise (channel=rgb keeps the three channels' bits in their own colours). In a natural image the low planes look like uniform noise; visible shapes, text, or a sharp boundary between "noisy" and "flat" areas in plane 0 indicate hidden data or synthetic editing (steganography inspection). With sheet=true all eight planes are written as one contact sheet (bit 7 top-left … bit 0 bottom-right). Also returns, per channel, the share of set LSBs and a pairs-of-values chi-square statistic (sequential LSB embedding pushes the share to 0.5 and chi-square per degree of freedom well below 1). PNGs with transparency are decoded bit-exactly.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

sheet.description: Write all 8 planes of the channel as a 4×2 contact sheet instead of a single plane

output.description: VFS path for the bit-plane image (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.compare
tools.description: Compare two images of the same size pixel by pixel. Returns MSE and PSNR (dB, over RGB; the string "Infinity" when the images are identical), mean SSIM on luma (structural similarity, 1 = identical; Wang et al. 11×11 gaussian window), the maximum channel difference, and the number and share of differing pixels; and writes a heat-map PNG showing where they differ (map=diff: largest channel difference per pixel, amplified; map=ssim: local SSIM, dark = dissimilar). Use for regression checks (did the render change?), to quantify compression loss, or to locate edits. If the sizes differ, pass resize=true to scale `b` to `a` first (Lanczos).

a.description: VFS path of the reference image

b.description: VFS path of the image to compare against it

resize.description: Resize b to the size of a when they differ (otherwise that is an error)

gain.description: Amplification of the diff map; 0 = automatic (largest difference becomes full scale)

colormap.description: Colour scale of the diff map

output.description: VFS path for the heat-map (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.components
tools.description: Count and measure the separate objects in an image. The image is binarised (Otsu by default, or a fixed luma threshold; set dark=true when the objects are darker than the background), connected regions are labelled (8- or 4-connectivity, two-pass union-find), and for each region you get its area in pixels, bounding box, centroid and extent (area ÷ bounding-box area). Writes a label map PNG with every component in its own colour. Use to count cells, coins, particles, stars, glyphs; to find the largest object; or to locate blobs for cropping. Clean the mask first with image.morph op=open if noise inflates the count, or raise minArea. The 50 largest components are listed.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

threshold.description: Luma threshold; omit for Otsu's automatic choice

dark.description: Objects are darker than the background (foreground = luma below the threshold)

minArea.description: Ignore components smaller than this many pixels (they are drawn dark gray in the label map)

output.description: VFS path for the label map (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.corners
tools.description: Detect corner points — places where the image changes strongly in two directions (junctions, tips, checkerboard crossings). method=shi-tomasi ("good features to track": smaller eigenvalue of the structure tensor, default) or harris (det − k·trace²). Returns the strongest corners with coordinates (in original pixels) and response, and writes an overlay PNG with the corners marked. Use for feature points to align or track images, to find the corners of a document or chart, or as a texture/detail measure. Images larger than maxSide are analysed downscaled.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

max.description: Maximum number of corners to detect (the JSON lists at most 100; all are drawn)

quality.description: Minimum response as a fraction of the strongest corner

minDistance.description: Minimum spacing between corners in (analysed) pixels

sigma.description: Gaussian integration scale of the structure tensor

maxSide.description: Analyse at this longer-side size at most

output.description: VFS path for the overlay (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.ela
tools.description: Error Level Analysis for tamper screening: the image is re-saved as JPEG at a known quality and the per-pixel difference from the original is amplified and written as a PNG. In an untouched JPEG the error level is fairly uniform for similar textures; regions pasted in or edited after the last save often stand out brighter (or darker). It is a hint, not proof: sharp edges and fine texture are always brighter, and PNG/lossless sources or heavily recompressed images are not informative. Returns the mean and maximum error and the grid cells with the highest error (as rectangles) so you can look closer.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

quality.description: JPEG quality of the re-save, in percent (90–95 is customary)

scale.description: Amplification of the difference; 0 = automatic (so the largest error is full scale)

output.description: VFS path for the error-level image (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.fft
tools.description: Two-dimensional Fourier spectrum of an image's luma, written as a PNG of log-magnitude with the zero frequency in the centre. The transform is exact for any width and height — no padding or cropping: power-of-two sides use radix-2 FFT, all other sides use Bluestein's chirp-z algorithm (the result says which). Bright spots away from the centre reveal periodic structure (halftone screens, moiré, sensor banding, JPEG 8-px blocking, repeating textures); the tool lists the most prominent spectral peaks with their frequency (cycles/pixel), period in pixels and orientation, and reports how much energy lies at high frequencies (low = blurry or upscaled). Images larger than `maxSide` are downscaled first (reported; periods are given in original pixels).

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

maxSide.description: Analyse at this longer-side size at most (memory: two f64 planes of that size)

window.description: Apply a Hann window first (removes the bright cross caused by the image borders; slightly widens peaks)

peaks.description: How many spectral peaks to report

output.description: VFS path for the spectrum image (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.histogram
tools.description: Brightness distribution of an image: per-channel histograms of R, G, B and Rec.709 luma (returned reduced to `bins` buckets), with mean, median, mode, the 1st/99th percentiles and the share of pixels clipped at 0 and 255 for each channel, plus a rendered chart PNG. Use it to judge exposure (clipped shadows/highlights), contrast (how much of the range is used) and colour casts (channels offset from each other).

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

bins.description: Buckets per channel in the returned JSON (the chart always uses all 256 levels)

scale.description: Vertical axis of the chart; log reveals sparsely populated levels

output.description: VFS path for the chart (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.lines
tools.description: Find straight lines with the Hough transform: Canny edges vote in (rho, theta) space (theta resolution 180/thetaSteps degrees, rho resolution 1 px) and local maxima of the vote count are lines. For each line you get rho/theta, the vote count, its direction angle (0° = horizontal, 90° = vertical, measured clockwise in image coordinates), and the endpoints and length of the longest stretch of edge pixels actually lying on it (in original pixels). Writes an overlay PNG with the segments drawn. Use to measure skew of a scanned page (take the dominant angle), find horizon/table/axis lines, or detect grid structure. Images larger than maxSide are analysed downscaled.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

minVotes.description: Minimum votes (edge pixels on the line); 0 = 30 % of the strongest line

maxGap.description: Largest gap in pixels bridged when measuring the supported segment

maxSide.description: Analyse at this longer-side size at most

output.description: VFS path for the overlay (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.lsbEmbed
tools.description: Hide a message in the least significant bits of an image (LSB steganography). Bits are written pixel by pixel in raster order, channels in R,G,B,A order, message bits most-significant first; by default a 4-byte big-endian length precedes the data. The output is always a lossless PNG (any lossy re-save destroys the message) and visually identical to the input (each used channel value changes by at most 2^bits − 1). The tool reads the result back and confirms the round trip. Capacity = pixels × channels × bits ÷ 8 bytes. Use analysis.lsbExtract with the same channels/bits/framing to recover it. This is concealment, not encryption.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

messageFile.description: VFS path of a file whose bytes to hide instead of `message`

channels.description: Channels carrying data, in R,G,B,A order: any of r g b a, e.g. "rgb", "b", "rgba"

bits.description: Low bits used per channel value (1 = classic LSB)

framing.description: How the message end is marked: length = 4-byte big-endian byte count before the data (this tool's default); nul = data ends at the first 0x00 byte (common in CTF tools); raw = no marker (extract reads maxBytes)

output.description: VFS path to write; must end in .png (default: <name>.stego.png)

tools.name: analysis.lsbExtract
tools.description: Recover data hidden in the least significant bits of an image (the inverse of analysis.lsbEmbed; also reads the common "sequential RGB LSB, MSB-first" layout of other tools with framing=nul or raw). Returns the message as text when it is valid UTF-8 (first 2000 characters), its byte length and the share of printable characters, and can write the raw bytes to a file. If framing=length finds an impossible length the image probably holds no message in that layout — try other channels/bits, or framing=raw to inspect the first bytes. PNGs with transparency are decoded bit-exactly.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

channels.description: Channels carrying data, in R,G,B,A order: any of r g b a, e.g. "rgb", "b", "rgba"

bits.description: Low bits used per channel value (1 = classic LSB)

framing.description: How the message end is marked: length = 4-byte big-endian byte count before the data (this tool's default); nul = data ends at the first 0x00 byte (common in CTF tools); raw = no marker (extract reads maxBytes)

maxBytes.description: Upper bound on bytes to read (the amount read for framing=raw; a cap for nul)

output.description: Optional VFS path to write the extracted bytes to

tools.name: analysis.noise
tools.description: Estimate the noise level (standard deviation, in 0–255 levels) of an image's luma with two classical estimators: Immerkær's fast method (Laplacian-difference mask; slightly high on heavily textured images) and the robust wavelet MAD estimator of Donoho (median of the finest diagonal Haar detail / 0.6745; resistant to edges). Both assume additive, roughly white noise; JPEG compression and denoising make them read low. Returns both values, a combined sigma (the smaller, as texture only inflates them) and a verdict.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

tools.name: analysis.palette
tools.description: Dominant colours of an image by k-means clustering (k-means++ seeding, deterministic for a given seed) in CIE L*a*b* (perceptual, default) or RGB. Returns up to k colours sorted by share: hex, RGB, proportion of pixels; and writes a swatch PNG whose bar widths are proportional to the shares. Fully transparent pixels are ignored. Large images are sampled evenly (≤ 200 000 pixels), which does not change the answer materially. Use to describe an image's colour scheme, pick theme colours, or check brand colours.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

seed.description: Seed for the k-means++ initialisation

output.description: VFS path for the swatch (PNG; default: derived from the input name)

tools.name: analysis.phash
tools.description: Perceptual fingerprints of an image, 64 bits each as 16 hex digits: aHash (8×8 average), dHash (9×8 horizontal gradient) and pHash (32×32 DCT, low 8×8 frequencies vs. their median). Unlike cryptographic hashes they change little under resizing, recompression and small edits. Give `compare` to also get the Hamming distance (0–64 differing bits) between the two images for each hash and a verdict (pHash distance ≤ 5 near-duplicate, ≤ 12 similar, else different — rules of thumb). Use for duplicate detection and "is this the same picture?" questions. The bit layout is this tool's own (row-major, MSB first); hashes are comparable with each other, not with other libraries.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

compare.description: VFS path of a second image to measure the distance to

tools.name: analysis.pixel
tools.description: Read the colour at a point, or the average colour of a rectangle: RGBA mean, hex, luma, and (for a rectangle) the per-channel min/max and standard deviation. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner. Use to verify a rendering ("is the button really #1a73e8?"), sample a background colour, or check whether a region is uniform.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

tools.name: analysis.sharpness
tools.description: Focus / blur measurement on luma: variance of the Laplacian (the standard blur detector — higher is sharper) and Tenengrad (mean squared Sobel gradient), plus a verdict. Thresholds are rules of thumb for natural photos near 1–2 MP (variance of Laplacian < 50 blurry, 50–150 soft, > 150 sharp); they depend on content and resolution, so to compare images use the same `maxSide`. By default the image is analysed at a normalised size (longer side ≤ 1024) so the numbers are comparable between files.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

maxSide.description: Analyse at this longer-side size (0 = full resolution)

tools.name: analysis.stats
tools.description: Summary statistics of an image: for R, G, B, alpha and Rec.709 luma the mean, standard deviation, min, max and Shannon entropy (bits, 0–8; low = flat, high = detailed/noisy); plus colourfulness (Hasler–Süsstrunk metric: <15 nearly gray, ~33 moderately, >80 very colourful), mean HSV saturation, and the share of near-black and near-white pixels. Use it for quick quality gates (is the image blank, washed out, monochrome?) and to compare images numerically.

input.description: VFS path of the source image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg — anything the browser decodes; max 40 megapixels)

tools.name: archive.create
tools.description: Create a zip, tar or tar.gz archive from VFS files: explicit paths and/or everything under a prefix. Entry names are the VFS paths with stripPrefix removed. Returns the archive file, entry count and compression ratio.

prefix.description: Also add every VFS file whose path starts with this prefix

output.description: VFS path of the archive; .zip, .tar, .tar.gz or .tgz decides the format

format.description: auto = from the output extension (zip when unknown)

stripPrefix.description: Remove this leading text from entry names (default: the prefix argument, when only prefix is used)

tools.name: archive.extract
tools.description: Extract a zip, tar, tar.gz/tgz or gzip file into the VFS under a prefix — everything, or only entries matching globs. Safe by construction: entries whose names contain ".." or a drive letter are refused (zip-slip) and reported, leading "/" is stripped, CRCs are verified, and extraction stops before exceeding maxBytes / maxFiles (zip-bomb guard, enforced on the real inflated size, not the declared one). Returns the extracted files (first 50), counts and anything refused or failed.

input.description: VFS path of the archive

prefix.description: VFS prefix to extract under (default: "<archive name>/"; "" = VFS root)

glob.description: Only extract entries matching these globs, e.g. ["*.csv", "docs/**"]

maxBytes.description: Refuse to produce more than this many decompressed bytes in total (zip-bomb guard; default 256 MiB)

maxFiles.description: Refuse to extract more files than this

strict.description: Fail the whole call if any entry has an unsafe name or cannot be read (default: skip it and report it)

flatten.description: Drop directories and extract by base name

tools.name: archive.gunzip
tools.description: Decompress a gzip file (or a zlib / raw deflate stream) into one VFS file, stopping with an error if the output would exceed maxBytes (decompression-bomb guard). For .tar.gz use archive.extract instead. Returns the decompressed file and what it looks like.

input.description: VFS path of the compressed file

output.description: VFS path (default: input without .gz/.zz, or <input>.out)

format.description: auto = detect gzip/zlib by header, else raw deflate

maxBytes.description: Refuse to produce more than this many decompressed bytes in total (zip-bomb guard; default 256 MiB)

tools.name: archive.gzip
tools.description: Compress one VFS file with gzip (or a raw zlib / deflate stream). Returns the compressed file and the ratio.

input.description: VFS path to compress

output.description: VFS path (default: <input>.gz, .zz for zlib, .deflate for raw deflate)

format.description: Container: gzip (RFC 1952), zlib (RFC 1950) or raw deflate (RFC 1951)

tools.name: archive.list
tools.description: List the entries of a zip, tar, tar.gz/tgz or gzip file without extracting: name, size, compressed size, method, modified time, plus flags for directories, encrypted entries and unsafe names (path traversal). Returns totals, the compression ratio and the first 50 entries (filter with glob); pass output to write the full listing as JSON.

input.description: VFS path of the archive

glob.description: Only entries matching these globs (* ? ** {a,b}); a pattern without "/" matches base names

maxBytes.description: Refuse to produce more than this many decompressed bytes in total (zip-bomb guard; default 256 MiB)

output.description: Optional VFS path for the complete listing (JSON)

tools.name: audio.channels
tools.description: Rearrange channels. op=mono: average all channels into one. split: write each channel as its own mono file. swap: exchange left and right. pick: keep one channel (index). dup: duplicate a mono file to stereo. merge: combine several mono files (inputs) into one multi-channel file. Returns the written file(s).

input.description: VFS path of the source audio (all ops except merge)

inputs.description: For op=merge: mono files in channel order (same sample rate; shorter ones are zero-padded)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.concat
tools.description: Join audio files end to end, with an optional silent gap or linear crossfade between them. Files are resampled to the first file's sample rate (or sampleRate) and mono files are duplicated to match a multi-channel one. Returns the joined file and each part's start time.

inputs.description: VFS paths in playback order (2 or more; the same path may repeat)

gap.description: Seconds of silence inserted between files

crossfade.description: Seconds of overlap with a linear crossfade between consecutive files (shortens the total; cannot be combined with gap)

sampleRate.description: Output sample rate (default: that of the first input)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.convert
tools.description: Convert audio to WAV (choose bit depth, sample rate, channel count) or, by delegation to video.transcodeAudio, to mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm. Also the way to extract the audio track of a video file as WAV. Returns the written file with duration, sampleRate and channels.

input.description: VFS path of the source audio (any decodable format, or a video with an audio track)

sampleRate.description: Resample to this rate in Hz (default: keep)

channels.description: Channel count: 1 = average to mono, 2 from mono = duplicate, 2 from 5.1 = ITU downmix (default: keep)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.dtmf
tools.description: Decode DTMF (telephone keypad) tones with Goertzel filters: returns the key string (0-9 A-D * #) and each key's start/end time. Tones should last at least ~40 ms with ~30 ms between repeats of the same key. Round-trips with audio.synth type=dtmf.

input.description: VFS path of the audio file

start.description: Start of the range to use, seconds (default 0)

end.description: End of the range, seconds (default: end of file)

minLevelDb.description: Ignore tone pairs quieter than this (dB re full scale, per tone)

maxTwistDb.description: Largest allowed level difference between the low and high tone of a key

tools.name: audio.fade
tools.description: Apply a fade-in at the start and/or a fade-out at the end of a file. Curves: linear, equalPower (sine), scurve (raised cosine), exp (slow start), log (fast start).

input.description: VFS path of the source audio

fadeIn.description: Fade-in length in seconds from the start

fadeOut.description: Fade-out length in seconds ending at the end of the file

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.filter
tools.description: Biquad (RBJ cookbook) filter: lowpass, highpass, bandpass, notch, peaking EQ, lowshelf, highshelf, allpass. sections cascades identical stages for a steeper slope (12 dB/octave each for low/high-pass); zeroPhase runs it forward and backward (no phase shift, attenuation doubled). Returns the file plus the filter's gain in dB at a few probe frequencies.

input.description: VFS path of the source audio

frequency.description: Cutoff / centre / shelf-midpoint frequency in Hz (must be below half the sample rate)

q.description: Quality factor: 0.707 = Butterworth for low/high-pass; higher = narrower band/notch/peak

gainDb.description: Boost or cut in dB for peaking, lowshelf and highshelf

sections.description: Number of identical cascaded biquad stages

zeroPhase.description: Filter forward then backward for zero phase distortion (squares the magnitude response)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.gain
tools.description: Change level by a fixed amount: gain in dB (or a linear factor), optional polarity inversion. Reports peak before and after so you can see whether the result clips. For level targets use audio.normalize.

input.description: VFS path of the source audio

db.description: Gain in decibels (+6.02 doubles the amplitude)

factor.description: Linear amplitude multiplier (alternative to db; negative inverts polarity)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

bitDepth.description: WAV sample format: 16 or 24 = integer PCM (clips above 0 dBFS), 32 = float (lossless for intermediates, keeps peaks above 0 dBFS). Default: same as a WAV input, else 16.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy compressed formats, e.g. 128 (passed to video.transcodeAudio; ignored for wav and flac)

tools.name: audio.info
tools.description: Identify an audio file: container and codec sniffed from the header bytes (wav, aiff, mp3, flac, ogg vorbis/opus, m4a/mp4, webm/mkv, adts), duration, sample rate, channels, bit depth, average bitrate (file bits ÷ duration) and tags (ID3v2/v1, Vorbis comments, MP4 ilst, RIFF INFO). Reads headers only unless they lack duration/rate/channels, in which case the file is decoded to measure them. Use first on any unknown audio file.

input.description: VFS path of the audio (or video-with-audio) file

probe.description: header = never decode; decode = always decode and report the exact decoded length; auto = decode only when the header is not enough

tools.name: audio.mix
tools.description: Sum several audio files into one (overdub / layering), each with its own gain in dB and start offset in seconds. Output length = the latest ending input. Reports the resulting peak; set normalize=true to scale the mix down when it would clip.

inputs.description: VFS paths to mix (2 or more)

gains.description: Gain per input in dB, same order as inputs (default 0 for each)

offsets.description: Start time per input in seconds within the mix (default 0 for each; must be ≥ 0)

normalize.description: If the summed peak exceeds −1 dBFS, scale the whole mix down to −1 dBFS

sampleRate.description: Output sample rate (default: that of the first input)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name). Its extension selects the format when "format" is not given.

format.description: Output format (default: from the output extension, else wav). wav is written natively; mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/opus/flac/webm are delegated to video.transcodeAudio and fail with a clear error if that tool is unavailable.

input.description: VFS path of the source audio

tools.description: Render a spectrogram PNG: time on the x axis (seconds), frequency on the y axis (linear, log or mel-spaced, labelled in Hz), colour = level in dB with a labelled colour bar. This is the main way for a vision model to "hear" a file: speech formants, notes, chirps, hum, clicks and dropouts are all visible. Returns the image plus the exact plot rectangle and axis ranges so pixels can be mapped back to seconds and Hz. input.description: VFS path of the audio file

start.description: Start of the range to use, seconds (default 0)

end.description: End of the range, seconds (default: end of file)

channel.description: "mix" (average), a 0-based channel index, or "all" for one stacked panel per channel (max 4)

fftSize.description: Window length in samples (default ≈ 40 ms: 2048 at 44.1/48 kHz). Smaller = sharper in time, blurrier in frequency

hop.description: Samples between columns. Default: chosen so the range fills the image width. If given, the plot becomes exactly one column per hop and width is recomputed (max 8192 columns)

minHz.description: Lowest frequency shown (default 0 for linear/mel, 20 for log)

dbRange.description: Dynamic range of the colour scale in dB below the top

dbMax.description: Level mapped to the brightest colour, dB re full-scale sine (default: the loudest value in the image)

colormap.description: magma / inferno / viridis (perceptually uniform), phosphor (green CRT), amber, gray (white = loud), ink (black on white, prints well)

output.description: VFS path of the PNG (default: <input>.spectrogram.png)

tools.description: Averaged FFT magnitude spectrum of a file or time range: the strongest spectral peaks (interpolated Hz, dB, nearest note), spectral centroid, spread, rolloff, flatness (0 = pure tone, 1 = white noise) and energy per octave or third-octave band. input.description: VFS path of the audio file

start.description: Start of the range to use, seconds (default 0)

end.description: End of the range, seconds (default: end of file)

channel.description: "mix" (average of all channels) or a 0-based channel index

peaks.description: How many of the strongest peaks to return (max 50)

bands.description: Band-energy table: octave (≈10 bands), third-octave (≈30 bands) or none

rolloffPercent.description: Rolloff = frequency below which this percentage of the energy lies

input.description: VFS path of the source audio

mode.description: resample = pitch follows speed; stretch = keep pitch (WSOLA)

Use it for 1-bit displays (e-paper, thermal printers), retro looks, or to avoid banding when lowering bit depth. Alpha is kept. To map onto specific colours use dither.palette instead. bayer2/4/8 at strength 1 can run on WebGPU.

tables.description: How to render <table>: GFM pipe table, raw HTML, fenced csv, or omitted. Tables that contain other tables are treated as layout and flattened.

tools.name: doc.info
tools.description: Identify a document and read its metadata without converting it. Sniffs the real type from magic bytes and content (not just the extension), then reports title/author/dates, counts that are knowable (words, slides, chapters, cells, cues, messages; "pages" only when the authoring app stored it) and the number of embedded media files. Also says which tool converts it: doc.toMarkdown for docx, pptx, odt, odp, epub, html, ipynb (Jupyter), rtf, eml, mbox, md, txt, srt, vtt; pdf.* for PDF; data.* for spreadsheets/CSV/JSON. Use it first when you are handed an unknown file.

input.description: VFS path of the document

tools.name: doc.media
tools.description: List, and optionally extract, the media files embedded in a zip-based document: docx, pptx, xlsx, odt/odp/ods, epub. Lists name, mime type and size of each embedded image/audio/video (fonts and other embedded objects on request). With extract=true the files are written under a VFS prefix so image.* / vision.* / audio.* tools can work on them. For images in reading order next to the text use doc.toMarkdown images=extract instead.

input.description: VFS path of the container document

extract.description: false = list only; true = also write the files to the VFS

kinds.description: Which kinds of embedded files to include

prefix.description: VFS prefix for extracted files (default: <input stem>_media)

tools.name: doc.subtitles
tools.description: Convert and retime subtitles: SRT ⇄ WebVTT, or to a plain transcript (txt / md) or a JSON cue list. Times can be shifted (shiftSeconds, negative = earlier; cues that end before 0 are dropped) and scaled (scale, e.g. 25/23.976 = 1.04271 to fix a frame-rate mismatch; applied before the shift). Transcripts merge cues into paragraphs, remove rolling duplicate lines from auto-captions and strip inline tags. Returns the output stat, cue count and duration.

input.description: VFS path of an .srt or .vtt file (format is sniffed from content)

to.description: Target: srt, vtt, txt (plain transcript), md (transcript with bold time stamps), json (array of {index,start,end,text} with times in seconds)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from input)

shiftSeconds.description: Add this many seconds to every time stamp (after scaling)

scale.description: Multiply every time stamp by this factor (before shifting)

stripTags.description: srt/vtt output: remove inline formatting tags (<i>, <b>, <c.class>, {\an8}…)

timestamps.description: txt/md output: collapse = one [hh:mm:ss] per paragraph, keep = one line per cue with its range, none = text only

tools.name: doc.toHtml
tools.description: Render a document as HTML. Markdown → HTML with GFM tables/task lists/strikethrough (marked); docx → HTML directly (mammoth, images embedded as data: URIs by default); every other doc.toMarkdown input goes through Markdown first. By default the result is a standalone page with a small embedded stylesheet — theme=light, or theme=terminal for a dark monospace look — and no external requests. Raw HTML inside Markdown is sanitised (scripts, iframes, event handlers and javascript: URLs removed) unless sanitize=false. Returns the output stat and title. For PDF output see pdf.fromMarkdown / pdf.* if registered.

input.description: VFS path: a Markdown file, a .docx, or anything doc.toMarkdown accepts

output.description: VFS path of the .html file to write (default: <input stem>.html)

theme.description: Embedded stylesheet: light (serif-less reading page), terminal (dark, monospace, green headings), none (no CSS)

standalone.description: true = full <!doctype html> page with <head>, charset and CSS; false = body fragment only

title.description: Page <title> (default: document title or first heading)

sanitize.description: Strip scripts, iframes, forms, on* handlers and javascript: URLs from the generated HTML

images.description: Embedded images of docx/pptx/epub…: inline = data: URIs (self-contained file), extract = separate files linked relatively, drop = removed. Image links in a Markdown input are left as they are.

tools.name: doc.toMarkdown
tools.description: Convert a document to clean Markdown an LLM can read, written to a .md file. One entry point for: docx, pptx, odt, odp, epub, html, ipynb (Jupyter), rtf, eml, mbox, md, txt, srt, vtt. docx keeps headings, bold/italic, lists, tables, links, footnotes and images; pptx/odp become one "## Slide N: title" section per slide with bullets, tables, pictures and speaker notes; epub chapters follow spine order; ipynb cells keep code fenced with the kernel language, text outputs and image outputs; eml/mbox give headers + body and extract attachments; srt/vtt become a readable transcript. Embedded images are written next to the .md (images=extract) and linked relatively. Returns the output file stat, detected type, title, metadata, an estimated token count and a short excerpt — read the file itself with fs.read, or plan with text.outline / text.chunk. Not for PDF (pdf.toMarkdown / pdf.* tools) or spreadsheets, CSV, JSON (data.convert / data.* tools): for those it fails with the tool to use.

input.description: VFS path of the source document (docx, pptx, odt, odp, epub, html, ipynb (Jupyter), rtf, eml, mbox, md, txt, srt, vtt)

output.description: VFS path of the .md file to write (default: <input stem>.md)

images.description: extract = write embedded images to imagesDir and link them relatively; inline = keep them as data: URIs inside the Markdown (large); alt = replace each image by its alt text; drop = remove images

imagesDir.description: VFS prefix for extracted images and email attachments (default: <output stem>_media)

tables.description:
markdown = GFM pipe tables (first row becomes the header, merged cells are un-merged, line breaks become
); html = keep raw HTML (html/docx/epub only); csv = fenced csv blocks; drop = omit tables

headingOffset.description: Shift every heading level by this amount (clamped to 1..6), e.g. 1 to nest the document under an existing H1

attachments.description: eml/mbox: extract = write attachments to imagesDir and link them; list = only name them

stripLinks.description: Keep link text but drop the URLs (html-based inputs: html, docx, epub, email HTML bodies)

type.description: Force the input type instead of sniffing it from magic bytes, extension and content

notes.description: pptx/odp: include speaker notes under each slide

timestamps.description: srt/vtt: collapse = merge cues into paragraphs with one [hh:mm:ss] stamp each; keep = one line per cue with its time range; none = paragraphs without times

mainContentOnly.description: html: keep only the main article (drops nav/aside/footer/ads, picks the densest article-like container)

baseUrl.description: html: URL the page came from; relative links and image sources are rewritten to absolute URLs against it

maxOutputChars.description: ipynb: cut each text output of a cell to this many characters (0 = no limit)

emailBody.description: eml/mbox: which body part to use; auto = text/plain when present, else the HTML part converted to Markdown

maxMessages.description: mbox: convert at most this many messages

tools.name: doc.toText
tools.description: Flatten a document to plain text (no Markdown syntax) and write a .txt file. Same inputs as doc.toMarkdown (docx, pptx, odt, odp, epub, html, ipynb (Jupyter), rtf, eml, mbox, md, txt, srt, vtt); headings become plain lines, list items keep "- " / "1. " markers, table rows become tab-separated lines, images are dropped (or replaced by "[image: alt]"). Use it for search indexing, embeddings or word counts where markup is noise; use doc.toMarkdown when structure matters. Returns the output stat, word/line counts, an estimated token count and a short excerpt.

input.description: VFS path of the source document (docx, pptx, odt, odp, epub, html, ipynb (Jupyter), rtf, eml, mbox, md, txt, srt, vtt)

output.description: VFS path of the .txt file to write (default: <input stem>.txt)

imageAlt.description: Keep "[image: alt text]" markers where images were

linkUrls.description: Append " (url)" after link text instead of dropping link targets

type.description: Force the input type instead of sniffing it from magic bytes, extension and content

notes.description: pptx/odp: include speaker notes under each slide

timestamps.description: srt/vtt: collapse = merge cues into paragraphs with one [hh:mm:ss] stamp each; keep = one line per cue with its time range; none = paragraphs without times

mainContentOnly.description: html: keep only the main article (drops nav/aside/footer/ads, picks the densest article-like container)

baseUrl.description: html: URL the page came from; relative links and image sources are rewritten to absolute URLs against it

maxOutputChars.description: ipynb: cut each text output of a cell to this many characters (0 = no limit)

emailBody.description: eml/mbox: which body part to use; auto = text/plain when present, else the HTML part converted to Markdown

maxMessages.description: mbox: convert at most this many messages

tools.name: encode.base32
tools.description: Base32 encode or decode (RFC 4648): the standard A–Z2–7 alphabet (TOTP secrets, onion addresses) or base32hex. File → file or inline. Decoding is case-insensitive and ignores padding, spaces and dashes.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

tools.name: encode.base58
tools.description: Base58 encode or decode with the Bitcoin alphabet (no 0, O, I, l) — as used by Bitcoin/Solana addresses and IPFS CIDv0. No checksum is added or verified (this is plain Base58, not Base58Check). Input is limited to 64 KiB. File → file or inline.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

tools.name: encode.base64
tools.description: Base64 encode or decode (RFC 4648), standard or URL-safe alphabet, with or without padding. Works file → file or on inline text. Decoding tolerates whitespace, missing padding, either alphabet and a data: URL prefix. Returns the result inline for inline text, or the written file.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

variant.description: Alphabet when encoding: standard (+/) or url (-_)

pad.description: Emit = padding when encoding (url variant usually omits it)

wrap.description: Insert a newline every N characters when encoding (0 = none; 76 = MIME)

tools.name: encode.charset
tools.description: Detect the text encoding of a file (BOMs for UTF-8/16/32, strict UTF-8 validation, UTF-16 without BOM by NUL pattern, otherwise a latin1/windows-1252 guess) and transcode it to UTF-8. Force the source encoding with from= (any WHATWG label: windows-1251, shift_jis, gbk, iso-8859-2 …) when the guess is wrong. Returns the detection with its evidence and confidence and the UTF-8 file. Single-byte code pages other than latin1/1252 cannot be auto-detected.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

from.description: Source encoding label, or auto to detect

detectOnly.description: Only report the detection, write nothing

newline.description: Normalise line endings in the output

bom.description: Write a UTF-8 BOM at the start of the output

output.description: VFS path of the UTF-8 result (default: <input>.utf8.<ext>)

tools.name: encode.hex
tools.description: Hex (base16) encode or decode. Encoding options: upper case and a separator between bytes. Decoding ignores whitespace, colons, commas, dashes and 0x prefixes. File → file or inline.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

separator.description: Text between bytes when encoding, e.g. " " or ":"

tools.name: encode.html
tools.description: Escape text for safe inclusion in HTML (& < > " ' → entities; optionally every non-ASCII character as a numeric reference), or decode HTML entities back to text (all named entities like é   … plus numeric é / é). Decoding does not strip tags. Inline or file → file.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

nonAscii.description: When encoding, also write non-ASCII characters as &#N; references

tools.name: encode.jwt
tools.description: Decode a JSON Web Token: header, payload (claims), signature length, and the time claims (iat, nbf, exp) as ISO timestamps with an expired flag. The signature is NOT verified — this only reads the token; never trust its claims on that basis.

token.description: The JWT (three base64url parts separated by dots; a "Bearer " prefix is tolerated)

input.description: VFS path of a file containing the token (instead of token)

tools.name: encode.url
tools.description: Percent-encode or decode text for URLs. mode=component (default) escapes everything except unreserved characters (use for one query value or path segment); mode=form is the same with spaces as "+" (application/x-www-form-urlencoded); mode=uri keeps URL structure characters (:/?#&=) intact. Decoding handles any of them. Inline or file → file.

input.description: VFS path to read (file → file: the result is written to output)

text.description: Inline text to encode, or inline encoded text to decode (instead of input)

output.description: VFS path to write. Default: derived from input for files; inline text returns the result inline (written to a file only when larger than 64 KiB)

tools.name: file.bitmap
tools.description: Render raw bytes as an image — binary visualisation: each byte becomes a grey pixel (or 3 bytes an RGB pixel, 4 RGBA, or each bit a black/white pixel), laid out in rows of a chosen width. Structure shows up visually: text looks like noise bands, zero padding is black, embedded uncompressed images appear when the width matches their stride. Returns the PNG (at most 16 M pixels; larger inputs are cut and flagged).

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

mode.description: gray = 1 byte/pixel, rgb = 3, rgba = 4, bits = 1 bit/pixel (MSB first)

length.description: Bytes to render (default: to the end)

scale.description: Integer upscale factor (nearest neighbour) for small inputs

output.description: VFS path of the PNG (default: <input>.bitmap.png)

tools.name: file.byteHistogram
tools.description: Count how often each byte value 0x00–0xFF occurs in a file and render it as a 256-bar PNG. Flat = random/encrypted; spikes at 0x00/0xFF = padding; mass in 0x20–0x7E = text. Returns the PNG plus the most common bytes, the number of distinct values and the zero / printable-ASCII / high-bit fractions.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

log.description: Logarithmic count axis (shows rare bytes next to dominant ones)

output.description: VFS path of the PNG (default: <input>.bytes.png)

tools.name: file.concat
tools.description: Concatenate several files byte for byte, in order, into one new file (rejoin split parts, prepend a header). Returns the new file and the offset where each part starts.

output.description: VFS path of the result (default: <first>.concat.<ext>)

tools.name: file.diff
tools.description: Byte-level comparison of two files at equal offsets (no insert/delete alignment): identical or not, offset of the first difference, number of differing bytes, similarity (matching bytes / longer length), and the differing ranges with a hex sample from each side (first 50; nearby ranges merge with mergeGap). Use it to see what a patch, a re-save or a corruption changed.

input.description: VFS path of the first file

other.description: VFS path of the second file

mergeGap.description: Merge differing ranges separated by at most this many equal bytes

tools.name: file.entropy
tools.description: Shannon entropy of a file in bits per byte (0 = constant, ~4–5 = text/code, >7.5 = compressed, >7.95 = encrypted or random), overall and per block, with the high-entropy regions listed by offset (runs of blocks at or above the threshold, which is lowered by the small-sample bias of the block size and reported as effectiveThreshold) — the standard way to spot packed, compressed or encrypted sections inside a binary. Also renders a PNG strip (entropy against file offset) for a vision model to look at. Returns the numbers, a 32-point profile and the PNG.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

blockSize.description: Bytes per block (default: 1024, or larger so the file has at most ~1024 blocks; 256 for files under 16 KiB)

threshold.description: Blocks at or above this entropy are reported as high-entropy regions

output.description: VFS path of the PNG (default: <input>.entropy.png)

tools.name: file.find
tools.description: Search a file for a byte pattern and return the offsets: a hex pattern with ?? wildcards ("89 50 4E 47", "FF D8 ?? E0"), a text string (UTF-8 or UTF-16LE, optionally case-insensitive), or a regular expression evaluated over the bytes as latin1 characters (so \x00 and [\x80-\xff] work). Returns the match count and the first matches with offset, length and a short context dump. Use it to locate signatures, embedded files or strings inside binaries.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

hex.description: Hex byte pattern; ?? matches any byte

text.description: Text to search for

regex.description: JavaScript regular expression source, matched against the bytes as latin1

encoding.description: text search: how the text is encoded in the file

context.description: Bytes of context shown after each match start

tools.name: file.hexdump
tools.description: Write a classic hex dump (offset, hex bytes, ASCII column — like `hexdump -C` / `xxd`) of a file or a byte range to a text file, and return its first lines inline. Dumps at most 4 MiB per call; page through larger files with offset/length.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

length.description: Bytes to dump (default: to the end, max 4 MiB)

output.description: VFS path of the dump (default: <input>.hex.txt)

tools.name: file.identify
tools.description: Identify what a file really is from its bytes (magic numbers and light structure checks), ignoring its name: ~150 formats across images, audio, video containers, archives, documents (PDF, Office/OpenDocument inside zip, OLE2), executables (PE, ELF, Mach-O, wasm, class), fonts, databases, and text kinds (JSON, XML, HTML, SVG, CSV, scripts, PEM…). Returns format, mime, usual extensions, category, a confidence 0–1, format details when cheap (PNG size, PE/ELF architecture, zip first entries) and extensionMatches=false with a warning when the file name lies about the content.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

tools.name: file.patch
tools.description: Edit bytes at an offset and write the result as a new file: overwrite in place (default), insert (shifting the rest), or delete a range. The new bytes come as hex, base64 or text. Returns the new file, the bytes that were replaced (hex) and the size change.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

hex.description: New bytes as hex, e.g. "DE AD BE EF"

text.description: New bytes as UTF-8 text

mode.description: overwrite = replace bytes in place (may extend the file); insert = add bytes, shifting the rest; delete = remove `length` bytes

length.description: delete mode: how many bytes to remove

output.description: VFS path (default: <input>.patched.<ext>)

tools.name: file.slice
tools.description: Copy a byte range of a file into a new file (carve out a header, an embedded payload, the tail). Negative offset counts from the end. Returns the new file and the exact range taken.

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

offset.description: First byte (negative = from the end, e.g. -128 for the last 128 bytes)

length.description: Number of bytes (default: to the end)

end.description: Exclusive end offset, alternative to length (negative = from the end)

output.description: VFS path (default: <input>.slice.bin)

tools.name: file.strings
tools.description: Extract runs of printable characters from a binary, like the Unix `strings` tool: ASCII and/or UTF-16LE runs of at least minLength characters, each with its byte offset. Optionally keep only those matching a regex (e.g. "https?://", "password"). Returns the first matches inline (default 50) and writes the full list to a text file ("offset<TAB>encoding<TAB>text", capped at 200 000 strings).

input.description: VFS path of the file to inspect

filter.description: Optional regular expression (case-insensitive) a string must match

maxLength.description: Truncate each inline string to this many characters

output.description: VFS path of the full list (default: <input>.strings.txt)

tools.name: fs.cp
tools.description: Copy a VFS file to a new path.

tools.name: fs.download
tools.description: Save a VFS file to the user's disk through a browser download.

filename.description: Suggested file name (default: the VFS name)

tools.name: fs.fetch
tools.description: Download a URL into the VFS. Subject to browser CORS: same-origin, data:/blob: URLs and CORS-enabled hosts work; others fail with a network error.

path.description: VFS path to save as (default: derived from the URL and content type)

tools.name: fs.list
tools.description: List files in the virtual file system (VFS). Every tool reads its inputs from and writes its outputs to the VFS by path. Each file reports `pipeline` (the source file it ultimately derives from), `from` (its direct inputs) and `by` (the tool that made it), so related outputs can be told apart from unrelated ones.

prefix.description: Only paths starting with this prefix

pipeline.description: Only files of the same pipeline as this path (everything derived from the same source file)

tools.name: fs.mv
tools.description: Rename a VFS file. The mime type follows the new extension only if you also convert it — this is a pure rename.

tools.name: fs.pipelines
tools.description: Group the VFS files by pipeline: each group is one source file followed by everything derived from it, in derivation order, with the tool that produced each step and its depth in the chain. Use it to see which outputs belong together, or pass `path` for just the pipeline that file is part of.

path.description: Only the pipeline containing this file

tools.name: fs.preview
tools.description: Show a VFS file in the page viewport (image, PDF page, video, audio, map, text, or hex) so a human or a screenshotting agent can look at it.

tools.name: fs.read
tools.description: Read a VFS file (or a byte range of it) back as text, base64, a data: URL, or a hex dump. Capped at 256 KiB per call — page through big files with offset/length.

encoding.description: auto = text for textual mime types, base64 otherwise

tools.name: fs.rm
tools.description: Delete VFS files by exact path, or everything under a prefix with all=true.

path.description: VFS path, or prefix when all=true

all.description: Treat path as a prefix and delete every match ("" wipes the VFS)

pipeline.description: Delete the whole pipeline this file belongs to (its source and everything derived from it)

tools.name: fs.stat
tools.description: Size, mime type and known metadata (width/height/pages/duration…) of one VFS file.

tools.name: fs.write
tools.description: Create or overwrite a VFS file from inline content: plain text, base64, or a data: URL. Use append=true to upload a large file in several base64 chunks.

path.description: VFS path to write; the extension decides the mime type

text.description: UTF-8 text content

base64.description: Base64 content (a data: URL prefix is tolerated)

append.description: Append to an existing file instead of replacing it

tools.name: geo.bbox
tools.description: Bounding box of a map file as [west, south, east, north], antimeridian-aware: data straddling ±180° (Fiji, the Aleutians, Pacific routes) gets a box with west > east instead of one spanning the whole globe. Also returns the centre and the box size in degrees and kilometres. Give output= to also write the box as a GeoJSON polygon.

input.description: VFS path of the map file. Accepted: GeoJSON (also newline-delimited), TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, WKT, CSV with lat/lon or WKT columns, encoded polyline text, Shapefile (.shp with its .dbf/.prj beside it in the VFS, or a .zip of them)

format.description: Input format. auto = sniff from the content (and extension)

layer.description: Only for multi-layer inputs: TopoJSON object name or shapefile name inside a zip (default: all layers; geo.info lists them)

output.description: Optional VFS path: write the box as a GeoJSON Polygon feature (nothing is written when omitted)

tools.name: geo.bearing
tools.description: Direction from one point to another in degrees clockwise from true north: the geodesic initial and final bearing (Vincenty, WGS84), the great-circle initial bearing on a sphere, and the constant rhumb-line (loxodrome) bearing with its length. Returns a 16-point compass name too.

from.description: Start point as [lon, lat] in degrees — longitude first (GeoJSON order), e.g. [-0.1276, 51.5072] for London

to.description: End point as [lon, lat] in degrees — longitude first (GeoJSON order), e.g. [-0.1276, 51.5072] for London

tools.name: geo.centroid
tools.description: Centre point of the whole dataset and of each feature: polygons by area, lines by length, points by mean — averaged on the sphere, so it is correct across the antimeridian. Returns the overall centroid and a per-feature list (capped by limit). Give output= to write the centroids as a GeoJSON point layer carrying the original properties (handy for labelling or for turning polygons into points).

input.description: VFS path of the map file. Accepted: GeoJSON (also newline-delimited), TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, WKT, CSV with lat/lon or WKT columns, encoded polyline text, Shapefile (.shp with its .dbf/.prj beside it in the VFS, or a .zip of them)

format.description: Input format. auto = sniff from the content (and extension)

layer.description: Only for multi-layer inputs: TopoJSON object name or shapefile name inside a zip (default: all layers; geo.info lists them)

output.description: Optional VFS path: write one Point per feature (nothing is written when omitted)

tools.name: geo.clip
tools.description: Cut geometry to a bounding box: points outside are dropped, lines are cut at the box edge (Liang-Barsky), polygons are trimmed to the box (Sutherland-Hodgman). Unlike geo.filter, features are actually cut, so nothing sticks out. A concave polygon that the box splits into several pieces stays one ring joined along the box edge. Returns features and vertices before/after.

input.description: VFS path of the map file. Accepted: GeoJSON (also newline-delimited), TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, WKT, CSV with lat/lon or WKT columns, encoded polyline text, Shapefile (.shp with its .dbf/.prj beside it in the VFS, or a .zip of them)

format.description: Input format. auto = sniff from the content (and extension)

layer.description: Only for multi-layer inputs: TopoJSON object name or shapefile name inside a zip (default: all layers; geo.info lists them)

bbox.description: Clip box as [west, south, east, north] in degrees. west > east means the box crosses the antimeridian

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input). GeoJSON unless the extension says otherwise (.geojson .topojson .kml .kmz .gpx .wkt .csv .polyline)

tools.name: geo.convert
tools.description: Convert a map file between formats, normalising it on the way. Reads GeoJSON, newline-delimited GeoJSON, TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX (tracks, routes, waypoints with elevation and time), WKT/EWKT, CSV (lat/lon columns or a WKT column, auto-detected), encoded polyline and Shapefile (.shp+.dbf+.prj, loose or zipped). Writes GeoJSON (default — a clean FeatureCollection that every other geo tool and any LLM can read), TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, WKT, CSV or encoded polyline. Shapefile cannot be written. Returns the output file plus notes on anything the target format could not hold.

input.description: VFS path of the map file. Accepted: GeoJSON (also newline-delimited), TopoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, WKT, CSV with lat/lon or WKT columns, encoded polyline text, Shapefile (.shp with its .dbf/.prj beside it in the VFS, or a .zip of them)

tools.name: geo.simplify
tools.description: Reduce the vertex count of lines and polygons so a dataset fits a model context or draws faster. Two algorithms: Douglas-Peucker ("dp", keeps points farther than the tolerance from the simplified line — best for tracks and roads) and Visvalingam-Whyatt ("visvalingam", removes the vertices spanning the smallest triangles — best for coastlines and borders). Give ONE of: tolerance (metres), targetVertices (absolute), ratio (fraction of vertices to keep). Line ends are always kept and rings never drop below 4 positions; each line is simplified on its own, so borders shared by neighbouring polygons may no longer match exactly. Returns vertices and bytes before/after.

tools.description: Time one image op on the GPU against the CPU on a synthetic image of a chosen size, to decide which backend is worth using here. GPU time is the kernel alone (upload + compute + readback, pipelines warm). CPU time comes from the public tool for that op run with backend=cpu when one is registered (then it includes PNG decode/encode, reported as cpu.via = tool name), otherwise from the built-in plain-JS reference kernel (cpu.via = "js-reference", kernel only). Returns ms (median of `runs`) for each side, the speed-up, and megapixels/s. Works without WebGPU (GPU side reported as unavailable).

Call this first to learn whether backend=gpu will work and how large an image the GPU accepts.

tools.name: gpu.run
tools.description: Apply one accelerated image kernel on the GPU, directly, and write the result as an image. WebGPU only (no CPU fallback — it fails with a clear error without a GPU; use the image.* tools for automatic fallback). Bytes are treated as linear values, edges clamp, alpha is kept unless the op says otherwise. Ops and their params: gaussian {sigma} — separable Gaussian blur of R,G,B; radius = ceil(3·sigma), weights normalised; the two passes are joined in floating point (no rounding in between). · convolve {kernel:number[size·size] row-major, size (odd, ≤25; default sqrt(kernel.length)), divisor=1, bias=0 (0..255 units)} — correlation (kernel not flipped): out = Σ k[j·size+i]·in(x+i−h, y+j−h) / divisor + bias on R,G,B. · sobel {} — Sobel gradient magnitude of Rec.709 luma (unrounded): sqrt(gx²+gy²) clamped to 255, written to R=G=B, alpha 255. · grayscale {} — Rec.709 luma 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B, rounded, written to R=G=B (computed exactly as (2126R+7152G+722B+5000) div 10000). · invert {} — 255−v on R,G,B. · threshold {t:0..255} — Rec.709 luma ≥ t → white, else black; alpha 255 (compared exactly as 2126R+7152G+722B ≥ 10000·t). · colorMatrix {matrix:number[20]} — 4×5 row-major like SVG feColorMatrix on straight 0..1 RGBA; column 5 is an offset in 0..1; alpha is computed by row 4. · resize {width, height, filter:"nearest"|"bilinear"} — pixel-centre aligned: source coordinate = (x+0.5)·sw/dw−0.5; nearest takes floor((x+0.5)·sw/dw); bilinear interpolates all four channels (no prefilter when shrinking). · morph {op:"erode"|"dilate", radius:int 1..128} — min (erode) or max (dilate) over a (2r+1)² square, per channel R,G,B. · bayer {levels:int 2..256, size:2|4|8, mono:bool} — ordered dither: threshold = (B[y%n][x%n]+0.5)/n²−0.5; out = round(clamp(v/255+threshold/(levels−1),0,1)·(levels−1))/(levels−1)·255; mono dithers Rec.709 luma and writes gray. Evaluated in exact integer arithmetic. · bilateral {sigmaSpace 0.5..25, sigmaColor 1..255} — edge-preserving blur, radius = ceil(2·sigmaSpace); weight = exp(−d²/(2σs²))·exp(−(ΔR²+ΔG²+ΔB²)/(2σc²)) with colour differences in 0..255 units.. Returns the output file stat, the normalised params and the time spent.

input.description: VFS path of the source image

params.description: Parameters of the op as an object (a JSON string is accepted too), e.g. {"sigma":3} for gaussian. Missing optional params take the documented defaults.

tools.name: gpu.shader
tools.description: Run your own WGSL over an image on the GPU — the playground tool. You write one function (or just its body): `fn pixel(p: vec2i, uv: vec2f) -> vec4f`, called once per output pixel; p = integer pixel coordinate (0,0 top-left), uv = pixel centre in 0..1; return straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA in 0..1, written to an 8-bit linear image (no sRGB conversion). Available to your code: `load(p)` exact texel of the source with clamp-to-edge · `tex(uv)` bilinear sample · `loadOrig(p)` / `texOrig(uv)` the same on the untouched input · `param(i)` the i-th of 8 float params · `u.resolution` (output size, px) · `u.srcSize` (input size, px) · `u.time` · `u.seed` · `u.frame` / `u.frames` (pass index / count). Raw bindings if you prefer: `src`, `orig` (texture_2d<f32>), `smp` (sampler). With passes>1 the output of each pass becomes `src` of the next (feedback, still 8-bit) while `orig` stays the input — iterate blurs, cellular automata, erosion. stage=fragment (default) allows derivatives (dpdx, textureSample); stage=compute runs the same contract in a compute shader (workgroup 8×8, textureStore). You may define helper functions and consts before `fn pixel`; do not declare bindings in group 0. Without an input the source is one transparent pixel: set width/height and generate procedurally. On a WGSL error nothing is written and the error lists every compiler message verbatim with the line:column in YOUR code and the offending line, so you can fix and retry. Example (edge glow): code = "let c = load(p).rgb; let dx = load(p + vec2i(1, 0)).rgb - load(p - vec2i(1, 0)).rgb; let dy = load(p + vec2i(0, 1)).rgb - load(p - vec2i(0, 1)).rgb; let e = length(dx) + length(dy); return vec4f(mix(c * 0.3, vec3f(0.2, 1.0, 0.4), clamp(e * param(0), 0.0, 1.0)), 1.0);" with params=[2]. Returns the output stat, stage, size, passes, ms and any compiler warnings.

Each output carries the page it was found on and its pixel size. Images repeated on several pages are written once; stencil masks and vector drawings are not images and are skipped. For a picture of a whole page use pdf.render.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages.

format.description: Output format (png is lossless)

quality.description: JPEG/WebP quality

minSide.description: Skip images whose shorter side is below this many pixels (icons, rules, spacers)

outputPrefix.description: Prefix for file names (default: input name); files are <prefix>.p<page>.img<k>.<ext>

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.info
tools.description: Inspect a PDF without changing it: page count, page sizes (points, with /Rotate applied), PDF version, metadata, encryption, whether pages carry a text layer (if not, it is a scan and needs OCR), fonts, image count and their share of the file size, and whether an outline, form fields or attachments exist. Use it first to decide between pdf.text / OCR and which pdf.compress mode can help.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

deep.description: Check every page for text (default: up to 40 evenly spaced pages)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.merge
tools.description: Concatenate several PDFs (optionally only some pages of each) into one PDF, in the order given. Returns the merged file with its page count and how many pages came from each input. Bookmarks, form-field definitions and document-level attachments are not carried into the new file (page content, links and annotations are).

inputs.description: VFS paths of the PDFs, in output order (a path may repeat)

ranges.description: Optional page selection per input, same order as inputs, e.g. ["1-3", "all", "2,5-"]

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <first input>.merged.pdf)

password.description: Password tried on every encrypted input

tools.name: pdf.metadata
tools.description: Read, set or strip a PDF's document metadata (title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, dates). With no fields and strip=false it only reads (no file written). Setting fields rewrites the Info dictionary and removes a stale XMP packet so viewers do not show old values; strip=true removes Info and XMP entirely (privacy clean-up). Returns the metadata after the change.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

keywords.description: Set the keywords (one string, comma-separated by convention)

strip.description: Remove all document metadata (Info dictionary and XMP) before applying any fields given

output.description: VFS path to write when something changes (default: <input>.meta.pdf)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.nup
tools.description: Impose several pages per sheet (2-up, 4-up, …) for printing or compact review: each source page is scaled as a vector (text stays text) into a grid cell on a new sheet. Returns the new PDF with its sheet count. Links, form fields and bookmarks are not kept.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages; order is honoured.

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.outline

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

output.description: Write mode: VFS path to write (default: <input>.outlined.pdf)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Pages that receive a label (default: all). Use "2-" to leave a cover page unnumbered.

tools.name: pdf.render
tools.description: Rasterise PDF pages to PNG, JPEG or WebP images at a given DPI or pixel width (pdf.js renderer; fonts, CJK cmaps, JPEG2000/JBIG2 and ICC colour supported). input.description: VFS path of the PDF

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

order.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). This is the new page order.

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input>.reordered.pdf)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.rotate
tools.description: Rotate pages of a PDF by a multiple of 90° (sets the page /Rotate flag — lossless, nothing is re-rendered; bookmarks and forms are kept). By default the angle is added to each page's current rotation.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages.

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.split
tools.description: Split one PDF into several: one file per page (default), a file every N pages, at given pages, or by explicit ranges. Bookmarks, form-field definitions and document-level attachments are not carried into the new file (page content, links and annotations are).

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

tools.name: pdf.text
tools.description: Extract the text layer of a PDF into a .txt file (best-effort reading order, one block per page) and return a short excerpt plus per-page character counts. Pages with no text layer (scanned images) are listed in pagesWithoutText — run OCR on a pdf.render of those pages instead. For headings/lists/tables use pdf.toMarkdown.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages.
