stripHeaders.description: Drop running headers/footers (lines repeated at the top/bottom of most pages)

excerptChars.description: Characters of text to return inline

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input>.text.txt)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.toMarkdown
tools.description: Convert a PDF with a text layer to Markdown using layout heuristics: headings from font sizes (and short bold lines), paragraphs re-flowed and de-hyphenated, bullet/numbered lists, monospace runs as code blocks, and simple tables where cells line up in columns. Heuristic — complex layouts, merged cells and multi-line table cells will not survive; images are not included (see pdf.images). Writes a .md file and returns counts plus an excerpt.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages.

pageMarkers.description: Insert "<!-- page N -->" comments at page starts

stripHeaders.description: Drop running headers/footers (lines repeated at the top/bottom of most pages, e.g. page numbers)

tables.description: Detect column-aligned rows and emit Markdown tables

order.description: Line order: stream (PDF emission order, keeps columns) or position (top-to-bottom, left-to-right)

excerptChars.description: Characters of Markdown to return inline

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input>.md)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: pdf.watermark
tools.description: Stamp text or an image on PDF pages — a diagonal "DRAFT"/"CONFIDENTIAL", a logo in a corner, or a tiled pattern — with opacity and rotation, over or under the page content. The page content stays intact (text remains selectable). Text uses a built-in font (WinAnsi only; other characters become "?"). Returns the stamped PDF.

input.description: VFS path of the PDF

text.description: Watermark text (give text or image)

image.description: VFS path of an image to use as watermark (PNG with transparency works)

pages.description: 1-based page selection such as "1-3,7,10-" ("10-" = to the end; also all, odd, even, last, "-5", reversed "5-1"). Default: all pages.

position.description: Where on the page; tile repeats it across the page

rotation.description: Degrees counter-clockwise (45 = rising diagonal; use 0 for corners)

fontSize.description: Text size in points (default: sized to span about 70% of the page for center, 5% of the page width otherwise)

color.description: Text colour (#rrggbb or a basic colour name)

scale.description: Image width as a fraction of the page width

margin.description: Distance from the page edge in points for edge/corner positions

layer.description: over = on top of the content; under = behind it (invisible where the page paints an opaque background, e.g. scans)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input>.watermarked.pdf)

password.description: Password, if the PDF is encrypted (user or owner password). Any PDF this tool writes is unencrypted — re-apply pdf.encrypt if needed

tools.name: speech.transcribe
tools.description: Speech-to-text with OpenAI Whisper running in the browser: turn any audio or video file in the VFS into text, with timestamps, in 99 languages (auto-detected), or translate foreign speech into English text. Use it for recordings, voice notes, podcasts, meetings, video soundtracks and subtitles. Any length: the audio is decoded to 16 kHz mono and walked through in 30 s windows, each new window starting where the last complete segment ended, so sentences are not cut and times are continuous. Always writes <name>.transcript.txt; on request also .srt and .vtt subtitles and a .json with every segment {start,end,text} (and words when timestamps=word). Returns the text (capped by maxChars, with a truncated flag), the language (and detection candidates), audio duration, real-time factor (processing time ÷ audio time; 0.1 = ten times faster than real time), the backend and quantisation actually used, load/run timings, downloadedBytes vs fromCache, and the output file stats. DOWNLOADS on first use of a model, from huggingface.co: whisper-tiny 122 MB (44 MB on CPU), whisper-tiny.en 122 MB (44 MB on CPU), whisper-base 209 MB (80 MB on CPU), whisper-base.en 209 MB (80 MB on CPU), whisper-small 589 MB (252 MB on CPU), whisper-small.en 589 MB (252 MB on CPU); plus the 29 MB runtime from this site. Speed measured on a desktop PC (RTX-class GPU, fast CPU core) on a 90 s clip: with WebGPU whisper-tiny runs 23×, whisper-base 19× and whisper-small 13× faster than real time (the first window after a load adds 0.5–3 s of shader compilation); on CPU (single-threaded WASM — this host cannot enable threads) whisper-tiny 12×, whisper-base 6.5×, whisper-small 2.3×; expect several times less on a laptop or phone. Word timestamps take about three times as long. Limits: greedy decoding; a window in which the decoder loops on a phrase is detected and decoded again with temperature 0.4 / 0.8 (reported as redecodedWindows, and repetitiveWindows when that did not help), but there is no no-speech or log-probability filter, so long silences or music can still yield invented text; word mode has no loop check; no speaker labels. Runs entirely in this page: the audio/prompt and the result never leave the browser. The only network traffic is the one-time download of model files from huggingface.co (and its CDN hosts under hf.co), cached afterwards in the browser (Cache API).

input.description: VFS path of the audio or video file (wav, mp3, flac, ogg/opus, m4a/aac, mp4, webm … whatever this browser's Web Audio decoder accepts)

model.description: Whisper model: whisper-tiny | whisper-tiny.en | whisper-base | whisper-base.en | whisper-small | whisper-small.en — tiny is fastest, small most accurate; ".en" variants are English-only and slightly better on English. Or any Hugging Face repo id with a Transformers.js Whisper export (e.g. onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo, ~1 GB — WebGPU only in practice). model.list has sizes and what this machine can run.

language.description: Spoken language as an ISO 639-1 code or English name ("es", "german"); auto = detect from the first 30 s. Give it when you know it: detection on tiny/base can be wrong for short or noisy clips.

task.description: transcribe = text in the spoken language; translate = English text from non-English speech (multilingual models only)

timestamps.description: segment = phrase-level times from Whisper's own timestamp tokens (reliable to about ±0.3 s). word = one time span per word from the decoder's cross-attention; this loads the separate "<model>_timestamped" export (same size, a second download), runs in 30 s chunks with 5 s overlap, is slower, and word boundaries are approximate (±0.1–0.3 s).

formats.description: Extra output files besides the .txt: srt and/or vtt subtitles, json = all segments (and words) with start/end seconds

start.description: Only transcribe from this second of the file (times in the outputs stay relative to the whole file)

end.description: Only transcribe up to this second of the file

backend.description: auto = WebGPU when a hardware adapter exists, else single-threaded WebAssembly (the result says which, and why a fallback happened); gpu = WebGPU or fail; cpu = force WebAssembly

dtype.description: Weight quantisation to load. auto picks per backend: speech → fp32 encoder + q4 decoder on WebGPU, q8 on CPU; llm → q4f16 on WebGPU with the shader-f16 feature (q4 without it, and always q4 for the Qwen2.5 models and for uncatalogued repos, whose 16-bit exports can produce garbage on WebGPU), q8 on CPU. Set it only to trade size for quality or for a repo that lacks the default file; the size figures in descriptions apply to auto.

maxChars.description: Cap on the text returned inline; the .txt file is never capped

output.description: VFS path of the text file (default: <input name>.transcript.txt); the other formats use the same name with their own extension

tools.name: synth.automaton
tools.description: Cellular automata as images. type=elementary: a 1-D Wolfram rule (0–255) drawn as a space-time diagram, one generation per row from the top (rule 30 chaos, 90 Sierpinski, 110 complex, 184 traffic). type=life: a 2-D life-like automaton (default Conway B3/S23, any B…/S… rule) started from seeded random soup and shown after N steps. Cells are drawn as `cell`-pixel squares, live = palette top, dead = palette bottom. Binary, structured, exactly reproducible — good for testing morphology, connected components and lossless compression. Returns the output stat, the grid size and the number of live cells in the final image.

type.description: elementary = 1-D rule over time; life = 2-D life-like rule after `steps` generations

cell.description: Pixel size of one cell; the grid is width/cell × height/cell cells

lifeRule.description: life: birth/survival rule in B/S notation, e.g. B3/S23 (Conway), B36/S23 (HighLife), B2/S (Seeds), B3/S12345 (Maze)

steps.description: life: number of generations to run

init.description: elementary: first row is a single live cell in the middle, or random. life always starts random

density.description: Probability that a cell starts alive in random initial states

wrap.description: Wrap around the edges (torus); otherwise cells outside are dead

seed.description: Seed — the same seed and arguments always give the same image

palette.description: Colour map applied to the scalar result. gray · phosphor (green CRT) · amber · fire · ice · viridis · magma · turbo · sunset · earth · rainbow · mono1 / phosphor1 / amber1 (1-bit, 8×8 Bayer-dithered)

output.description: VFS path to write; the extension picks png (default, lossless), jpg or webp. Default: <generator>.png, numbered if taken

tools.name: synth.checker
tools.description: Checkerboard with exact, unantialiased cells of a given pixel size and two colours. Known geometry for testing resizing (aliasing), corner/edge detection, camera-style calibration, and as a transparency background. Returns the output stat and the number of columns/rows of cells.

cell.description: Cell side in pixels (1 gives the highest-frequency pattern an image can hold)

cellHeight.description: Cell height if different from cell

offsetX.description: Horizontal shift of the pattern in pixels

output.description: VFS path to write; the extension picks png (default, lossless), jpg or webp. Default: <generator>.png, numbered if taken

tools.name: synth.gradient
tools.description: Colour gradient: linear (any angle), radial (any centre/radius) or conic (angular sweep), through any number of colour stops, optionally repeated. Interpolation is plain per-channel RGBA on byte values (no gamma), computed exactly — a clean ramp for testing banding, dithering, quantisation and colour-space conversions. Returns the output stat and the resolved stops.

stops.description: Colour stops in order: CSS colours, each optionally followed by a position 0..1 or a percentage, e.g. ["#000", "#f80 0.3", "white 100%"]. Unpositioned stops are spread evenly

angle.description: linear: direction in degrees (0 = left→right, 90 = top→bottom). conic: start angle (0 = +x axis, clockwise on screen)

centerX.description: radial/conic centre x as a fraction of the width

centerY.description: radial/conic centre y as a fraction of the height

radius.description: radial: radius where the last stop is reached, as a fraction of min(width,height)/2 (default: reach the farthest corner)

repeat.description: Number of times the stop sequence repeats across the gradient extent

mirror.description: When repeating, reflect every other repetition (no seams)

output.description: VFS path to write; the extension picks png (default, lossless), jpg or webp. Default: <generator>.png, numbered if taken

tools.name: synth.julia
tools.description: Render the Julia set of z → z² + c for a chosen constant c = cRe + i·cIm, with smooth escape-time colouring; points that never escape are black. Returns the output stat, backend, precision and inside fraction.

cRe.description: Real part of the constant c

cIm.description: Imaginary part of the constant c

centerX.description: Real coordinate at the image centre

centerY.description: Imaginary coordinate at the image centre (positive is up)

zoom.description: Magnification: the image height spans 3/zoom units of the complex plane

iterations.description: Maximum iterations; raise it when zooming in (boundaries stay blobby otherwise)

period.description: Colouring: iterations per palette sweep. The smooth escape count runs through the palette forward then backward every 2·period iterations

palette.description: Colour map applied to the scalar result. gray · phosphor (green CRT) · amber · fire · ice · viridis · magma · turbo · sunset · earth · rainbow · mono1 / phosphor1 / amber1 (1-bit, 8×8 Bayer-dithered)

tools.name: synth.mandelbrot
tools.description: Render the Mandelbrot set (z → z² + c from z = 0) around any centre at any zoom, with smooth (continuous) escape-time colouring through a palette; points inside the set are black. Endless fine structure with sharp filaments next to flat areas — a good stress image for compression, scaling and edge detection. WebGPU computes in 32-bit floats (fast, fine up to a zoom of a few thousand); past that, backend=auto switches to the float64 JS path. Returns the output stat, the backend and precision used, and the fraction of pixels inside the set.

zoom.description: Magnification: the image height spans 3/zoom units of the complex plane

period.description: Colouring: iterations per palette sweep. The smooth escape count runs through the palette forward then backward every 2·period iterations

output.description: VFS path to write; the extension picks png (default, lossless), jpg or webp. Default: <generator>.png, numbered if taken

tools.name: synth.maze
tools.description: Perfect maze (exactly one path between any two cells) carved by a seeded depth-first search: white corridors, black walls, entrance at the top-left, exit at the bottom-right. Hard-edged orthogonal structure with a known answer — use it for path-finding, skeleton/thinning, morphology and connected-component tests (the corridors form exactly one component). palette.description: Colour map applied to the scalar result. gray · phosphor (green CRT) · amber · fire · ice · viridis · magma · turbo · sunset · earth · rainbow · mono1 / phosphor1 / amber1 (1-bit, 8×8 Bayer-dithered)

output.description: VFS path to write; the extension picks png (default, lossless), jpg or webp. Default: <generator>.png, numbered if taken

tools.name: synth.moire
tools.description: Moiré interference: two overlaid gratings (straight lines, concentric circles, or radial spokes) multiplied together; the second is rotated, rescaled and shifted relative to the first, which produces the low-frequency beat fringes. tools.name: synth.noise
tools.description: Generate a noise image: white (independent per pixel), value, perlin (gradient), simplex or worley (cellular, distance to the nearest feature point), with fractal octaves (fBm). The JS and WebGPU paths implement the same hash and bases, so both backends give the same picture (within float rounding). Returns the output stat, the backend used and the field min/max/mean before normalisation.

octaves.description: Number of fBm octaves summed (1 = the plain basis)

offsetX.description: Pan in pixels (scroll the infinite noise plane horizontally)

tools.name: synth.reactionDiffusion
tools.description: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion: two virtual chemicals U and V diffuse and react (U + 2V → 3V) on a torus, growing organic Turing patterns — corals, dividing spots, mazes, worms — from a few seeded squares. The image shows the concentration of V after `steps` iterations. Presets (feed, kill): coral (0.0545, 0.062), mitosis (0.0367, 0.0649), spots (0.03, 0.062), maze (0.029, 0.057), worms (0.078, 0.061), holes (0.039, 0.058), waves (0.014, 0.045), fingerprint (0.037, 0.06); or set feed/kill yourself. Patterns need a few thousand steps; WebGPU runs them in well under a second, the JS path takes seconds (it refuses jobs above ~3·10⁹ cell-steps). Both paths run the same float32 scheme, but the system amplifies rounding differences, so backends agree in character, not pixel for pixel. Returns the output stat, backend, the parameters used and the mean of V.

preset.description: Named (feed, kill) pair; explicit feed/kill override it

kill.description: Kill rate k of V (overrides the preset)

tools.name: synth.scene
tools.description: A photo-like landscape composite built to exercise filters the way a real photograph does: a smooth sky gradient with a glowing sun and soft fractal clouds (low frequencies, banding-prone), layered mountain silhouettes (strong irregular edges, atmospheric haze), a textured field with perspective furrows (fine detail, frequency sweep), a building with a regular window grid, a round sign on a pole and thin wires (hard edges, periodic detail, 1-px lines), lens vignetting and Gaussian sensor noise. Fully seeded; the result reports where the main elements are (horizon, sun, building, sign) so you can crop them or check detectors. Use it wherever you would otherwise need "some photo".

tools.name: synth.shapes
tools.description: Scatter separate solid shapes — circles, axis-aligned rectangles, irregular blobs — on a flat background, and return the ground truth: the exact number of shapes and, for each, its kind, pixel area, centroid and bounding box. Shapes are unantialiased and never touch each other or the border (at least `gap` pixels apart), so a correct connected-components / blob-counting / object-detection run on this image must find exactly `count` objects. Use it to validate analysis.components, thresholding, contour and measurement tools. If the canvas is too crowded to place every requested shape, `count` is the number actually drawn (and `requested` the number asked for). Optional Gaussian noise makes the task harder.

color.description: Shape colour: any CSS colour, or "random" for a different bright colour per shape (each has Rec.709 luma ≥ 80)

noise.description: Standard deviation of Gaussian noise added to every pixel (0 = clean)

duty.description: square only: fraction of the period that is colorB

phase.description: Shift of the pattern as a fraction of a period

tools.name: synth.testcard
tools.description: Television-style test card with known content, for checking any conversion, filter or codec: 8 colour bars (white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, black at 100% or 75%), a continuous gray ramp, a stepped gray wedge, line gratings of period 2–16 px (vertical and horizontal), a Siemens star, R/G/B/gray ramps, 1-px and 2-px checkerboards, a zone plate and a 1-px white frame. The result lists every region as {name, x, y, w, h} and the exact bar colours, so you can sample the processed image and compare numerically.

tools.description: Render a string to an image with the browser's text engine — ground truth for OCR and text-detection tests, or a quick label/caption maker. Multi-line (use \n), optional word-wrap to a fixed width, any CSS font family, size, colours, alignment; rotation and Gaussian noise make recognition harder on purpose. With no width/height the image is sized to fit the text. The result returns the exact lines drawn and the bounding box of the ink. Glyph shapes depend on the fonts installed on this machine, so pixels (not content) can differ between machines.

tools.description: Truchet tiling: a grid of square tiles, each randomly put in one of two orientations (seeded). style=arcs gives the classic meandering quarter-circle paths, lines the diagonal labyrinth ("10 PRINT"), triangles the original half-filled tiles. Curved and diagonal antialiased strokes on a regular grid — useful for testing line/contour tracing, thinning and texture analysis. Returns the output stat and the tile grid size.

tools.name: synth.zoneplate
tools.description: Circular zone plate: v = 0.5 + 0.5·cos(π·k·r²), concentric rings whose spatial frequency grows linearly with the distance from the centre, reaching `frequency` cycles/pixel at the nearest image edge. Every frequency and orientation in one image — the standard chart for judging resizers and filters: aliasing shows up as phantom ring systems, blur as grey-out from the rim inward. Returns the output stat and the radius at which a given frequency is reached.

tools.name: sys.env

With domain or query: matching tools with one-line descriptions. sys.help gives one tool's full schema; sys.rooms lists the other rooms.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to search in names and descriptions

tools.name: text.chunk
tools.description: Split a text or Markdown file into chunks that each fit a token budget, for retrieval or for feeding a long document to a model piece by piece. Cuts prefer, in order: a heading, a paragraph / code-block / table boundary, a line, a sentence, a word — a hard character cut happens only inside a single unbroken token run longer than a quarter of the budget. Fenced code blocks are kept whole when they fit. Optional overlap repeats the tail of each chunk at the start of the next. Every chunk is an exact byte slice of the source, so concatenating the chunks (each minus its first overlapBytes bytes) reproduces the file. Writes NNNN.<ext> chunk files plus manifest.json under a prefix; returns the manifest head (index, path, heading path, estimated tokens, byte range). Token counts use the text.stats heuristic (not a real tokenizer — leave ~30% headroom below a hard model limit).

input.description: VFS path of the text/Markdown file

maxTokens.description: Budget per chunk in estimated tokens (overlap included); no chunk exceeds it

overlapTokens.description: Estimated tokens repeated from the end of the previous chunk (at most half of maxTokens; aligned to sentence/line boundaries, so the actual overlap is ≤ this)

markdown.description: Treat # headings, fenced code and tables as structure. auto = yes for .md/.markdown files, and for other files that contain ATX headings

prefix.description: VFS prefix for the chunk files (default: <input stem>.chunks)

tools.name: text.dedupe
tools.description: Remove duplicate lines from a text file, keeping the first occurrence and the original order (unlike sort -u). Options: compare case-insensitively, ignore surrounding whitespace, only collapse adjacent repeats (like uniq), keep blank lines. Returns lines in/out, how many were removed and the most repeated lines.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input stem>.dedupe.<ext>)

ignoreCase.description: Lines differing only in case are duplicates

trim.description: Ignore leading/trailing whitespace when comparing (the first occurrence is kept as written)

adjacent.description: Only remove a line when it repeats the line directly before it

keepBlank.description: Never remove blank lines (keeps paragraph structure)

tools.name: text.diff
tools.description: Line-based unified diff of two text files (Myers algorithm), written as a .diff file that `patch` / `git apply` understand. Returns added/removed/unchanged line counts, hunk count, a 0–1 similarity ratio and the head of the diff. Line endings are compared as LF. If the files differ by more than 3000 edit steps in their changed middle the diff falls back to one big replace hunk and sets approximate=true. Use ignoreWhitespace / ignoreCase to hide noise.

a.description: VFS path of the old / left file

b.description: VFS path of the new / right file

context.description: Unchanged lines shown around each change

ignoreWhitespace.description: Treat lines that differ only in whitespace as equal

output.description: VFS path of the .diff file (default: <a stem>.diff; not written when the files are identical)

tools.name: text.extract
tools.description: Find entities in a text file by pattern: emails, urls (http/https/ftp), dates (ISO 8601, 31/12/2024-style, English month names), numbers (with thousands separators, decimals, exponents, %), hashes (hex strings of MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 length), ips (IPv4 and IPv6, validated), uuids, phones (7–15 digits with common separators). Returns, per kind, the total and unique counts and the values with their frequencies, most frequent first, capped at limit. Pattern-based: expect some false positives (e.g. version numbers among numbers, order numbers among phones) and no understanding of context.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

kinds.description: Which entity kinds to look for

limit.description: Max distinct values returned per kind

output.description: Optional VFS path for the full uncapped result as JSON

tools.name: text.grep
tools.description: Search text files with a regular expression (or literal text), line by line, like grep -n. Give one file (input), several (inputs), or every text file under a VFS prefix. Returns up to maxMatches matching lines with path, line and column, the matched text, capture groups and optional context lines, plus total and per-file counts. Lines longer than 10 000 characters are searched only in their first 10 000. Guard against runaway regexes: the search runs in a Worker killed after timeoutMs; binary files are skipped; at most 64 MiB of text per call.

input.description: VFS path of one text file

prefix.description: Search every text file whose path starts with this prefix

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression source (no slashes), or plain text when literal=true. Max 2000 characters.

literal.description: Treat pattern as plain text, not a regex

flags.description: Extra regex flags: m (^/$ match per line), s (dot matches newline), u (unicode). i via ignoreCase; g is managed by the tool

timeoutMs.description: Kill the search after this long. The regex runs in a Worker that is terminated at the deadline, so a catastrophically backtracking pattern fails with an error instead of freezing the page.

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match

invert.description: Return lines that do NOT match

maxMatches.description: Max matching lines returned (counting continues past the cap)

tools.name: text.normalize
tools.description: Clean up a text file: unify line endings, apply Unicode normalisation (NFC by default; NFKC also folds full-width forms, ligatures and superscripts), strip control and zero-width characters, optionally turn smart quotes, dashes, ellipses and non-breaking spaces into plain ASCII, collapse runs of spaces and blank lines, trim trailing whitespace, expand tabs. Returns the output stat and a count of each kind of change, so you can see what was wrong with the file.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input stem>.normalized.<ext>)

stripControl.description: Remove C0/C1 control characters (except tab and newlines), zero-width and bidi marks, soft hyphens, stray BOMs

asciiQuotes.description: Curly quotes → ' and ", en/em dashes → - and --, … → ..., non-breaking and thin spaces → space

collapseWhitespace.description: Runs of spaces/tabs inside a line → one space (indentation is kept), 3+ line breaks → one blank line, trailing whitespace trimmed

trimTrailing.description: Remove spaces and tabs at line ends

tabs.description: Replace each tab with this many spaces (0 = keep tabs)

finalNewline.description: Make sure the file ends with a line break

tools.name: text.outline
tools.description: Heading tree of a Markdown file with an estimated token count per section — use it to decide which parts of a long document to read. Each entry has level, title, line number, ownTokens (the section body up to the next heading), tokens (including its sub-sections) and a byte range you can pass straight to fs.read (offset=byteStart, length=byteEnd-byteStart). Recognises ATX (#) and setext (=== / ---) headings and ignores fenced code. Token counts are the text.stats heuristic, not a real tokenizer.

input.description: VFS path of the Markdown file

maxDepth.description: Deepest heading level to list (deeper sections still count in their parents)

tools.name: text.redact
tools.description: Mask personal-looking data in a text file and write the redacted copy: email addresses, phone numbers, credit-card-like numbers (13–19 digits passing the Luhn check), IPv4/IPv6 addresses. Returns a count per kind. This is PATTERN-BASED redaction: it does not find names, postal addresses, IDs, or anything phrased unusually, and it can mask look-alikes (order numbers, version strings). Treat the output as reduced-risk, not anonymised; review before sharing.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input stem>.redacted.<ext>)

mask.description: label = [EMAIL] / [PHONE] / [CARD] / [IP]; stars = same-length ****; numbered = [EMAIL_1], [EMAIL_2]… with the same value always getting the same number (keeps who-is-who readable)

tools.name: text.replace
tools.description: Regex (or literal) search-and-replace over a whole text file, written to a new file; the source is left untouched unless output names it. The replacement supports $1…$99, $<name>, $& (whole match) and $$ like JavaScript String.replace; all matches are replaced. Returns the number of replacements and the output stat. Same runaway-regex guard as text.grep: runs in a Worker killed after timeoutMs.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression source (no slashes), or plain text when literal=true. Max 2000 characters.

literal.description: Treat pattern as plain text, not a regex

flags.description: Extra regex flags: m (^/$ match per line), s (dot matches newline), u (unicode). i via ignoreCase; g is managed by the tool

timeoutMs.description: Kill the search after this long. The regex runs in a Worker that is terminated at the deadline, so a catastrophically backtracking pattern fails with an error instead of freezing the page.

replacement.description: Replacement text; $1, $<name>, $& and $$ are expanded unless literal=true. Empty string deletes the matches.

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input stem>.replaced.<ext>)

tools.name: text.sort
tools.description: Sort the lines of a text file. Modes: alpha (Unicode code-point order, or locale-aware with ignoreCase), natural ("file2" before "file10"), numeric (by the first number on each line; lines without a number go last), length. Options: reverse, unique (drop exact duplicates after sorting), keep a number of header lines in place, drop blank lines. The sort is stable. Returns the output stat and line counts.

input.description: VFS path of the text file

output.description: VFS path to write (default: <input stem>.sorted.<ext>)

unique.description: Remove duplicate lines (after case folding when ignoreCase=true)

headerLines.description: Leave this many leading lines unsorted at the top

tools.name: text.stats
tools.description: Measure a text file: bytes, characters, words, lines, paragraphs, sentences (approximate), reading time, a language and script guess, and an estimated LLM token count. The token figure is a character-class heuristic, NOT a real tokenizer: its weights were fitted to OpenAI cl100k/o200k counts on ten sample texts, where it landed within ±5% on English prose and between −19% (JSON) and +19% (code-heavy docs) overall; it was not measured against Claude tokenizers, which usually count more tokens — use it to budget context with headroom, not to bill. Language is guessed from scripts plus stop-word frequency for 13 Latin-script languages; null when unsure.

input.description: VFS path of a text file (txt, md, csv, json, code…)

tools.name: video.capabilities
tools.description: What this browser can do with video/audio: per codec (h264, hevc, vp8, vp9, av1; aac, opus, mp3, vorbis, flac, pcm) whether WebCodecs can decode and encode it, separately for any/hardware/software implementations (VideoEncoder/VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported at the given resolution), which audio encoders come from bundled WASM instead, which containers each backend writes, and whether the ffmpeg.wasm fallback is reachable. Use it to choose codecs before converting.

width.description: Resolution to test video codecs at (hardware encoders have size limits)

height.description: Resolution to test video codecs at

loadFfmpeg.description: Actually download and start ffmpeg.wasm (~31 MB) to prove it loads and report its version; default only checks that the files are reachable

tools.name: video.compress
tools.description: Make a video file smaller. Either give targetMB (the bitrate is computed from the duration, the picture is scaled down automatically when the budget is too tight, and the encode is repeated once or twice if it overshoots) or a preset (low ≈ 480p, medium ≈ 720p, high ≈ 1080p, never upscaling). Output is mp4/h264+aac unless format says otherwise. Returns {output, before, after, ratio, savedPercent, targetMet?, attempts, backend, hardwareAccelerated, video, audio}. Limits: everything is held in browser memory — WebCodecs handles inputs up to ~1900 MB (practically a few hundred MB), the ffmpeg backend up to 1024 MB of input and a 2 GB WebAssembly heap, and is 5–50× slower (CPU, one thread).

input.description: VFS path of the source video

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name); its extension selects the container when format is not given

targetMB.description: Maximum output size in megabytes (MiB). Takes precedence over preset

preset.description: Quality preset used when targetMB is not given

format.description: Target container; auto = from the output extension, else mp4

videoCodec.description: auto = container default (h264 for mp4, vp9 for webm). hevc/av1 compress better where the browser can encode them (see video.capabilities)

maxWidth.description: Cap the output width (never upscales); overrides the automatic choice

fps.description: Reduce the frame rate as well

audioBitrate.description: Audio bitrate in kbit/s (default 96, or 64 when the size target is tight)

backend.description: auto = WebCodecs (hardware-accelerated where the browser offers it), falling back to ffmpeg.wasm (CPU) when WebCodecs cannot do the job; webcodecs / ffmpeg force one and fail instead of falling back

hardware.description: WebCodecs only. auto = use a hardware codec when one exists; hardware = require it (fails if none); software = force CPU codecs (slower, sometimes better quality at low bitrates)

tools.name: video.concat
tools.description: Join several videos end to end into one file. mode=reencode (default) decodes every clip and re-encodes onto one canvas (size of the first clip unless width/height are given; others are letterboxed), so clips may differ in codec, size and frame rate; clips without audio get silence. mode=copy joins without re-encoding (ffmpeg concat demuxer) and requires all clips to share codec, resolution and audio layout. Returns {output, backend, hardwareAccelerated, clips, duration, video, audio}. Limits: everything is held in browser memory — WebCodecs handles inputs up to ~1900 MB (practically a few hundred MB), the ffmpeg backend up to 1024 MB of input and a 2 GB WebAssembly heap, and is 5–50× slower (CPU, one thread).

inputs.description: VFS paths of the clips, in playback order

output.description: VFS path to write (default: derived from the input name); its extension selects the container when format is not given

mode.description: reencode = works for any mix of clips; copy = lossless and fast but only for same-format clips (ffmpeg backend)

format.description: Target container; auto = from the output extension, else that of the first clip, else mp4

videoCodec.description: Video codec when re-encoding (auto = container default)

width.description: Output width in pixels (rounded to even). With only width or only height the aspect ratio is kept

height.description: Output height in pixels (rounded to even)

fps.description: Force a constant output frame rate (default: keep each clip's own timing)

scale.description: Resample the image (or region) by this factor before recognition. Tesseract works best when capital letters are 20–40 px tall: use 2–3 for small screen text, below 1 for very large scans.

whitelist.description: Restrict recognition to these characters, e.g. "0123456789.-" for numbers (default: no restriction). Other characters are dropped, not substituted, and the reported confidence is not meaningful (often 0) when a whitelist is set.

preserveSpaces.description: Keep runs of spaces between words (useful for column-aligned tables)

dpi.description: Tell Tesseract the resolution of the image (default: let it estimate)

boxes.description: Also return bounding boxes {x,y,width,height} in input-image pixels with per-item confidence: per text line or per word. Writes the full list to <name>.ocr.json.

formats.description: Extra output files: hocr (HTML with layout and boxes) and/or tsv (Tesseract table: level, box, confidence, text). Coordinates in these two files are in pixels of the processed image (after region crop and scale), not of the input.

maxChars.description: Cap on the text returned inline; the .txt file is never capped

output.description: VFS path for the text file (default: <input name>.ocr.txt)

tools.name: vision.ocrOverlay
tools.description: Run OCR (same engine and options as vision.ocr) and draw what was found onto a copy of the image: one rectangle per word (or line), coloured by confidence (green ≥ 85, orange 60–84, red < 60), with the recognised text printed above each box. Use it to check visually what the OCR read and where, or to debug a bad result before changing psm/scale/region. Returns the annotated PNG in the VFS plus text, mean confidence and counts. When scale > 1 the picture is enlarged by the same factor (overlayScale) so labels stay legible; on tightly spaced lines the labels cover part of the line above — pass labels=false for boxes only. Same first-use download as vision.ocr (about 5 MB).

input.description: VFS path of the image (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, avif, svg). For a PDF page, render it to an image first.

language.description: Language model(s) to use; several may be combined (e.g. eng,deu). Bundled: eng=English, deu=German, fra=French, spa=Spanish. Other languages are not available.

level.description: Draw one box per word or per text line

labels.description: Print the recognised text above each box

tools.name: vision.qrRead
tools.description: Decode QR codes in an image (QR, Micro QR and rMQR only — a faster, stricter vision.barcodeRead). Returns each code's text, bounding box, corner points, error-correction level and version; several codes per image are supported. Use vision.barcodeRead for other symbologies. First use downloads 1.5 MB.

input.description: VFS path of the image containing one or more codes

region.description: Only look inside this rectangle: x,y,width,height in input-image pixels (default: whole image). Returned coordinates are still in whole-image pixels.

tryHarder.description: Spend more time: also try rotated (90/180/270°) and downscaled versions of the image. Turn off only for speed on clean, upright codes.

tryInvert.description: Also look for inverted (light on dark) codes

denoise.description: Apply a morphological closing before 2D detection — helps with noisy or dotted prints, slower

bytes.description: Also return the raw payload bytes as base64 (always included for binary payloads; capped at 3000 bytes)

annotate.description: Also write a copy of the image with every detected code outlined and labelled (result.output)

output.description: VFS path for the annotated image when annotate=true (default: <input name>.barcodes.png)

tools.name: vision.qrWrite
tools.description: Make a QR code (PNG or SVG) from text or a URL — shorthand for vision.barcodeWrite format=QRCode. Options: size in pixels, quiet-zone margin, error correction L/M/Q/H (use H when the code will be printed small or overlaid with a logo). Returns the file stat, module count and scale. First use downloads 1.5 MB.

text.description: Payload as text (UTF-8). Numeric-only symbologies need digits: EAN13 12–13, EAN8 7–8, UPCA 11–12, UPCE 7–8, ITF an even count; a missing check digit is computed, a wrong one is an error.

base64.description: Binary payload as base64, instead of text (2D symbologies)

size.description: Target size in pixels of the longer side; the largest whole number of pixels per module that fits is used, so the result is at most this size and always crisp. Ignored when scale is given.

margin.description: Quiet zone around the symbol in modules. -1 = the standard quiet zone of the symbology (QR 4, Data Matrix 1, linear codes 10…); 0 = none (not reliably scannable).

ecLevel.description: Minimum error correction (raised for free when the symbol has spare capacity): L ≈ 7 %, M ≈ 15 %, Q ≈ 25 %, H ≈ 30 % of the code can be damaged and still read

humanReadable.description: Print the payload as text under the bars (linear codes)

rotate.description: Rotate the symbol clockwise by this many degrees

invert.description: Light modules on a dark background

as.description: Output file type (default: from the output extension, else png)

output.description: VFS path to write (default: qrcode.png)
